study type: Model-development study based on historical national data analysis
exposure: Phase of maternal, stillbirth, and neonatal mortality transition
Health workforce density and skills mix
Service coverage (first antenatal care visits, four or more antenatal care visits, institutional births, caesarean section rates)
cohort: The study analysed UN estimates for 151 countries and 326 national surveys to assess changes in mortality indicators and associated characteristics.
finding: The study identified a five-phase maternal, stillbirth, and neonatal mortality transition model, demonstrating that progression through these phases is associated with declining infectious disease and peripartum deaths, lower fertility, and improvements in health workforce, financing, and increased service coverage, including institutional births.
mod_finding: Progression through mortality transition phases was associated with a significant increase in institutional births (from 36% to 99%) and rising caesarean section rates (from 2% to 25%), with earlier transitions driven by lower-level institutional births and later stages by rapid increases in hospital births.
